quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle to escape if needed. Eye contact alone is not enough for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if you need to.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. If traffic is coming toward you, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your crash risk, you should:
questions.explanation: Be as visible as possible by wearing bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Before getting on a motorcycle, you should check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals. You do not need to check for paint damage.

questions.question: To reduce your crash risk, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible, tell other drivers what you are doing, keep safe distance around you, look 12 seconds ahead, spot hazards, and be ready for changing conditions.

questions.question: All of the following reduce accident risk except:

options.text: Spotting hazards and planning which ones to handle first.

questions.explanation: To lower your crash risk, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide which to address first. Always use your headlight and keep space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: The best riding formation for a group is:
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. Switch to a single-file line when turning, riding through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or on your helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it during both day and night.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate during a wobble as it will make the motorcycle less stable. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Lean forward and down, and pull off the road when safe. Avoid braking as it may worsen the wobble.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: The pass may be completed in a no passing zone.
The rider may travel up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
The pass must be started and completed within a passing zone.
The pass must be completed on the shoulder, if one is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pass must be started and completed within a passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must start and finish passing only in areas where passing is legal and safe. You must follow the speed limit during the pass.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders who wear helmets.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do about lane position?

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of a lane.
Always avoid the right portion of a lane.
Always avoid the center portion of a lane.
Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions. There is no single position you should always avoid.

questions.question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) level is considered legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent is the legal intoxication limit. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: How long should a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.explanation: Do a thorough inspection of your motorcycle before every ride. This usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: What does an experienced rider do with lane position?

options.text: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
Stays in one portion of a lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Travels only on the oily portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes positions within their lane as conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle rider has three lane position options. Choose the safest position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in a lane position that makes you visible to the driver.
Always ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Not be concerned about your placement.
Always ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a lane position that makes you visible to the driver.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. This position is most visible in the driver's rearview mirror.

questions.question: How should you brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab at the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab at the rear brake.
Press down on the front brake and jam on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.
